sentences.text: It is the case of the prosecution is that the accused No.1 was applied the loan amount for Rs.53 lakhs at Punjab National Bank, Hudson Circle, Okkaligara Bhavana, 1st Floor, Bengaluru to purchase machinery for Arjun Packaging Company and the bank sanctioned the said loan amount to the accused No.1.

The accused No.1 was availed the said loan amount by producing fraudulent and created collateral security fake blue prints documents of house bearing No.434, Gokul, Mattikere, 1st Stage,
Bengaluru as genuine documents to the said bank which was belongs to the accused No.3 and 4.

Thereafter, the accused persons did not repay the loan amount to the bank and thereby the accused persons caused loss to the bank and cheated the complainant and thereby they have committed the above offences.
After completion of the investigation the P I of S.R.Nagara police station has filed the charge sheet against the accused persons 406, 420, 120(B), 471 read with section 34 of IPC 3.
Thereafter, the complainant has lodged the complaint in S.R.Nagara Police station.
In turn they have registered the case under Crime No.0022/2008.
Thereafter, police visited the spot, drew the mahazar, secured in the presence of the Accused persons subsequently were enlarged on bail.
Thereafter, on completion of the investigation, I.O. has submitted the charge sheet against the Accused persons for the above said offences.
After filing the charge sheet, Court has taken cognizance of the offences against the Accused persons and has issued summons to them.
4. The accused have appeared before the court through their counsel.
Copy of the prosecution papers were furnished under Section 207 of Code of Criminal procedure.

Thereafter, heard both side, the charges against the accused No.1 to 4 were framed for the offences punishable 406, 420,
120(B), 471 read with section 34 of IPC.

Read over and explained to the accused No.1 to 4 were pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
5.
To substantiate the case of the prosecution, the prosecution have examined the three witnesses as PW-1 to PW- 3 and got marked the 7 documents as Exs.P-1 to Ex.P-3.
The accused have did not choose to lead defense evidence.
The statement of the accused No.1 and 3 under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., is duly recorded.

6. Heard the arguments from both side and perused the deposition and documents.
7.
After hearing the parties and on perusal of records, the following points arose for my consideration.

1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 dated 24.10.2002 within jurisdiction of SR Nagar Police Station at Punjab National Bank at Okkaligara Bhavana he applied the loan application to the Arjun Packaging Company for the amount of Rs.53 lakhs the accused No.3 and 4 for the purpose collateral security and submitted the blueprints of the house belongs to the accused No.3 and 4 by believing that they have originals and obtained the loan amount of Rs.53 lakhs and made illegal profit without repaying the loan amount to the bank and thereby accused persons have committed criminal breach of trust and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 406 read with section 34 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the above said date, place and time the accused persons took the loan amount of Rs.53 lakhs from the CW-1 bank for the purpose purchase the machinery and they did not repay the loan amount to the bank intentionally made the criminal conspiracy and thereby accused persons have committed offence punishable under section 120(B) read with section 34 of IPC?

4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the above said date, place and time the accused persons applied the application for the loan amount of Rs.53 lakhs from the CW-1 bank for the purpose of purchase the submitted the forged house blueprints of sale deed as genuine documents for the purpose of collateral security and they did not repay the loan amount to the bank and thereby accused persons have committed offence punishable under section 471 read with section 34 of IPC?

To bring the home the guilt of accused persons the prosecution has to prove the ingredients of Under Section 406 of IPC.

Sec. 406 of I P C Reads as follows:
Section 406 : Punishment for  criminal breach of trust.- Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with both.
3. Accused (i) misappropriated, (ii) converted to his own use, (iii) used or disposed off that property or willful suffered any person to dispose off that property.
4. Accused did in violation of (i) any direction of law, (ii) any legal contract express or implied relating to carrying out the trust.
5. He did so dishonestly.

5 15.
To bring the home the guilt of accused persons the prosecution has to prove the ingredients of Under Section 420 of IPC.

Sec. 420 of I P C Reads as follows:
Section 420 : Cheating and  dishonestly inducing delivery of  property.-

Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
1. Essential ingredients are as follows;
1. Accused cheated the complainant.
2. Accused did so dishonestly.
3. Thereby induced the complainant:
(i) to deliver some property to accused or to some other person.
(ii) to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of the valuable security or anything which was signed, sealed, and which was capable of being converted into valuable security.

2. One of the ingredients of cheating as defined in Section 415 of the Indian Penal Code is existence of an intention of making initial promise or existence thereof from the very beginning of formation of contract.
S.V.L. Murthy v. State Rep.

By CBI, Hyderabad, 2009 (4) Supreme 399 : 2009 (7) JT 385 : (2009) 6 SCC 77 : (2009) 2 SCC (Crl) 941 : AIR 2009 SC 2717.
3. To constitute an offence under section 420, there should not only be cheating, but as a consequence of such cheating, the accused should have dishonestly include the person deceived (I)
to delivery any property to any person, or (ii) to make, alter or destroy wholly or in part a valuable security (or anything signed or sealed and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security).

Md. Ibrahim v. State of Bihar, 2009 (6) Supreme 470 : 2009 (11) JT 533:
2009 (4) Crimes 13 : (2009) 3 SCC (Crl) 929.

Using as genuine a forged [document or electronic record].- Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any [document or electronic record] which he knows or has reason to believe to be a forged [document or electronic record], shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such [document or electronic record] Ingredients.

(iv) He knew or had reason to believe that  it is forged.

2. Essential ingredients is knowledge or belief that it is forged.
17. To bring the home the guilt of accused person the prosecution has to prove the ingredients of Under Section 120(B) of IPC.

Sec. 120(B) of I P C Reads as follows.-
Punishment of criminal conspiracy.-

(1) Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, [imprisonment for life] or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall, where no express provision is made in this Code for the punishment of such a conspiracy, be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence.

(2) Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine or with both.

Ingredients of criminal conspiracy Circumstances in a case, when taken together on their face value,
should indicate meeting of minds between the conspirators for the intended object of committing an illegal act or an act which is not illegal, committed by illegal means.
A few bits here and a few bits there on which prosecution relies cannot be held to be adequate for connecting the accused with the commission of the crime of criminal conspiracy.
It has to be shown that all means adopted and illegal acts done were in furtherance of the object of conspiracy hatched.
Circumstances relied for the purposes of drawing an inference should be prior in point of time than the actual commission of the offence in furtherance of the alleged conspiracy.
18. Further it is important to note that except the CW-2, CW-3 and CW-12 as examined as PW-1 to 3 the prosecution failed to secure the other witnesses.
Hence, the CW-1, 4 to 11, 13 and 14 were dropped.

19. The PW-1 is the Mahazar witness who was deposed in his chief examination that from 2003 to 2008 he was on duty as a Senior Manager in Punjab National Bank at Okkaligara Bhavana,
Bengaluru.
The witnesses identified his signatures in spot mahazar and his signature marked as Ex.P-1(a).
He further deposed that the accused persons gave the fake documents to the bank and obtained a total loan amount of Rs.53 lakhs.
He further deposed that he put his signature when the bank filed the complaint against the accused persons.
20. The PW-1 deposed in his cross examination that he don't remember what time the Ex.P-1 was conducted.
He further deposed that at that time Rajan and Parameshwar were present.
He don't remember the other persons.
21. The PW-2 is the mahazar witness who was deposed in the chief examination that from 2008 to 2010 he worked as a Senior Manager in Punjab National Bank, Hudson Circle, Bengaluru.
That on 19.02.2008 the Sampangiramanagara Police came to our branch for panchanama.
He further deposed that before that V.Gujjal who was the Assistant Manager and he said that he had come to the panchanama on the basis of complaint.
At that time they got the account details of Arjun Packaging.
After the completion of panchanama they get his signature.
The mahazar drawn at 11.20 am to 12.30 pm.
The witnesses identified his signature in the Ex.P-1 and his signature is marked as Ex.P-1(b).
22. The PW-2 deposed in his cross examination that the Police have not issued a notice to him to cooperate the panchanama.
But they came to the branch and informed orally.
But he don't know their names.
He can't say who were present at the time of panchanama and remained witnesses at the time of Panchanama.
23. The PW-3 who is the investigation officer.
He deposed in the chief examination that from September 2007 to August 2008 he worked as PSI at Sampangiramanagara Police Station.
That on 19.02.2008 at 10.30 am when he was in station the CW-1 came to the Police station and lodged the complaint.
As per the complaint Crime No.72/2008 was registered after he submitted the FIR to the Court.
The witnesses identified the complaint which is marked as Ex.P-2 and his signature is marked as Ex.P-2(a).

The witnesses identified the FIR which is marked as Ex.P-3 and his signature V.Gujjal vs M.Vijaykumar And Others on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127900557/
8 marked as Ex.P-3(a).
On the same day in the presence of the CW-2 and 3 the mahazar was drawn from 11.20 am to 12.20 pm.
24. The PW-3 deposed in his cross examination that the complainant came to the Police station dated 19.02.2008.
Due to that day he took the complaint.
He did not issued notice to the CW-2 and 3.
He admitted that he did not seized the any articles in the spot.
He can't say the schedule of the incident place.
He denied the suggestion that deposed the false evidence against the accused persons.
25. The accused No.2 and 4 reported as died.

Hence case abated against the accused No.2 and 4.
26.
In the instant case the PW-1 deposed in his cross examination that he don't remember what time the Ex.P-1 was conducted.
The PW-2 deposed in his cross examination that he can't say who were present at the time of panchanama and remained witnesses at the time of Panchanama.
The PW-3 deposed in his cross examination that he admitted that he did not seized the any articles in the spot.
He can't say the schedule of the incident place.
27. In this case, the prosecution has failed to elicit anything favorable to it to prove the allegations U/Sec.406, 420, 120(B) and 471 read with section 34 of IPC.
When these being the facts, I am of the opinion that in total the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubt.
In view of the same, this court hold Point No.1 to 4 in the Negative.
28. Point No.5: For the reasons stated and finding given to point No.1 to 4, the following is made.

ORDER The accused No.1 and 3 are not found guilty for the offences punishable under section 406,
420, 120(B) and 471 read with section 34 of IPC.
Acting under section 248(1) of Code of are hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under section 406, 420, 120(B) and 471 read with section 34 of IPC.
The bail bonds and surety bonds executed by them stand canceled.
